author: Zoppox
quote:
Great visuals, locations, and cool looking bosses. Combat feels like an upgrade from the older games thanks to Ashes of War plus jumping/crouching attacks. The soundtrack is good enough. That’s where the good stuff ends. 

60 fps lock on a game released in 2022, are we trolling? Still no dlss or framegen support. Without Lossless scaling program I wouldn't even bother playing it.

The worst part of the game is the empty, repetitive open world. Base game is around 160 hours if you explore everything, DLC another 48. In that same time you could finish Demon’s Souls, DS1–3 and Bloodborne and get 5x more actual content. Most of those hours are just riding around checking under every rock for a cave or illusory wall so you can find another weapon or sorcery you can’t use, or more hefty bones, beast blood, claws and teeth, I bet most people have no Idea what you can even craft with them, yet they are majority of the loot in the game. 80% of the loot is this trash (plus souls you can farm from normal enemies anyway). 
Exploring also punishes you. If you clear every optional boss before the main boss in the area you will be so over leveled that almost nothing can kill you. The first bosses that actually took me more than one try were Radahn, Rykard, the double gargoyles, and everything after Fire Giant. Until then I was bored out of my mind for 130+ hours. I dropped the game twice and when returned only forced myself through it 2 hours a day and it felt like a job and a chore. I did it only because I respect the older FromSoft titles too much to leave it unfinished. After Limgrave I installed a mod that boosted enemy health, resistances and damage by 25% and played whole game with it and I was still bored out of my mind. Then I just wanted to play the game and have some fun, only to come across wizard towers with stupid puzzles like hunting down multiple turtles swinging off a cliff or tree somewhere across a massive area. Also, it's ridiculous that 208 hours of gameplay are just filled with trash AFK zombies, dogs, and rats who pose absolutely no threat. They serve no purpose and bring nothing to the game but boredom. The only time this felt like a proper Souls game was the area before Consort Radahn. Only that brief moment was challenging and engaging outside of boss battles.

Story is basically nonexistent. I’m not watching 6 hour YouTube videos to decode what some NPC’s fart supposedly meant. Quest interactions are annoying: exhaust dialogue, reload the area a few times, then the NPC teleports somewhere you’ve already cleared. Without Google you’ll miss most of it. Killing boss Rycard killed like 5 questlines for me, just a fantastic game design.

Minor complaint: why is there a massive compass in the middle of the screen 100% of the time with no option to turn it off? (had to mod it away).  The only reason to use it maybe to find your place of death easier, but you probably should just remember where you died?

This game could have been a 9/10 if they cut 70% of the open-world bloat and useless loot, kept the base game under 70 hours, and just sent you from castle to another castle or to cave to city, frequently fighting actual unique bosses, properly balanced around your expected level for this location instead of the same ones copy-pasted 60 times. For people who want the suffering add an optional hard mode (like DS2’s Covenant of Champions) or reduce soul gain massively and you lose all souls on death or something. Have just a normal dialogue with npc's with start and finish, and tell an engaging story.

author: Zoppox
quote:
Finished it solo on Brutal. The top-down combat and bosses are the best I’ve ever seen. Also good builds variety and you can change everything on the fly. Soundtrack, voice lines, graphics, and overall atmosphere are all really good.

The late game is where it loses some steam. Act 4 gets roughly four times more grindy: juggling ~15 crafting stations with resources that you need to collect from different corners of the map, managing 8 servants and their gear, and 3+ prisoners (good blood types being pure RNG) starts feeling like a busywork. Farming the same incursions repeatedly for the best weapons and passives (basically mandatory for endgame bosses) also dragged, even with max yield it took me 3+ hours of mindless grind for last 2 items of my set.

Not sure it’s even possible to finish Brutal pure melee. Something like Necesse’s Resilience system (stacking shield the more you attack, with higher stacks from melee) would make melee a lot more viable imo.

Wish there was a simple toggle to change world settings for better single player experience and some new features like an item that let's you setup teleport anywhere (so dying to a boss doesn’t mean a 5-minute run through packs of mobs) would make the single-player experience a lot smoother. Optimization could also use some work.

Despite the minor annoyances, it’s still a top-tier game.

author: Zoppox

Satisfying combat. Great graphics. Good difficulty. Good story. Good platforming.
Minus 2 points for annoying puzzles and occasional stutters and bad fps drops, and bugs.

author: Zoppox
quote:
+ for idea and realization of crawling on walls as an insect. This is unique and fun and got me into the game
+ Graphics and levels are fine. Also there is some story and some puzzles I guess.
- And that's it, nothing else in this game and game is 4-5 hours long. It got too boring at 3h for me and I uninstalled.

author: Zoppox
quote:
I enjoyed this soulslike a lot. Maybe will even replay it one day. I mostly like the atmosphere. It's a scary and brutal place, and after unlocking another shortcut you glad to be in this safe room again and listen to this beautiful song playing and just chill and do upgrades.
I disliked how game encourages you to play with one weapon type whole game, to upgrade it's stats more.
Near the end of the game and a bit in the middle, there was an annoying vertical maze of a level, with like five different elevators inside walls and it was impossible to tell where you will end up and where you need to go.
Last boss was too easy
